name: Data Lake and Analytics
description: A pattern for centralising data from multiple sources into a scalable data lake for analytics, reporting, and data science workloads. Supports structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data with governance controls appropriate for government data handling requirements.
whenToUse: Centralising data from multiple departmental systems for cross-cutting analytics
Building management information and performance reporting capabilities
Enabling data science and machine learning workloads on organisational data
Creating a single source of truth for operational and strategic reporting
Supporting open data publication requirements with appropriate governance
whenNotToUse: Simple reporting needs that can be met by existing BI tools connected to source systems
Real-time operational dashboards requiring sub-second data freshness
Small datasets that fit comfortably in a single relational database
Scenarios where data governance and cataloguing overhead is disproportionate
Transactional workloads requiring ACID guarantees across the dataset

typicalComponents.name: Data Lake Storage
typicalComponents.purpose: Store raw and processed data at scale in open formats
typicalComponents.technology: S3, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, or Cloud Storage

typicalComponents.name: Data Catalogue
typicalComponents.purpose: Discover, classify, and govern data assets across the lake
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Glue Data Catalog, Azure Purview, or Dataplex

typicalComponents.name: ETL/ELT Engine
typicalComponents.purpose: Extract, transform, and load data from source systems into the lake
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, or Dataflow

typicalComponents.name: Query Engine
typicalComponents.purpose: Run SQL queries against data lake files without loading into a database
typicalComponents.technology: Amazon Athena, Azure Synapse, or BigQuery

typicalComponents.name: BI and Visualisation
typicalComponents.purpose: Create dashboards and reports for business users

typicalComponents.name: Data Quality Framework
typicalComponents.purpose: Validate data quality rules and flag anomalies
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Glue DataBrew, Azure Data Quality, or Great Expectations

securityControls: Implement column-level and row-level security for sensitive data access
Encrypt all data at rest using platform-managed or customer-managed keys
Implement data classification tagging aligned to government security classifications
Apply lake-level access policies with IAM roles per data zone (raw, curated, published)
Implement data masking and tokenisation for PII in analytics environments
Audit log all data access queries and export operations
resilienceConsiderations: Object storage provides inherent durability (11 nines) without additional configuration
ETL pipelines should be idempotent and restartable from the last checkpoint
Implement data versioning to enable rollback of incorrect transformations
Query engines are stateless and can be restarted without data loss
Cross-region replication for disaster recovery of critical datasets
costConsiderations: Storage costs scale with data volume — implement lifecycle policies for cold data
Query costs depend on data scanned — partition and compress data to reduce costs
ETL compute costs incurred during processing windows only
BI tool licensing costs per user or per capacity unit
Consider the cost of data governance tooling and catalogue maintenance
Implement cost allocation tags to charge back to data-owning teams
operationalConsiderations: Data governance framework must be established before ingesting data
Data stewardship roles needed for each data domain
ETL pipeline monitoring for failures, data quality issues, and SLA breaches
Capacity planning for query concurrency during peak reporting periods
Data retention policies must comply with departmental and legal requirements
Training needed for analysts and data scientists on lake tools and governance

services.name: Amazon S3
services.purpose: Scalable data lake storage with lifecycle management

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.purpose: Serverless SQL queries on S3 data

services.name: AWS Lake Formation
services.purpose: Data lake governance and access control

services.name: Azure Synapse Analytics
services.purpose: Unified analytics with SQL and Spark

services.name: Cloud Storage
services.purpose: Data lake storage with object lifecycle

questionsToAsk: What data sources need to be ingested and what are their formats and volumes?
Who are the primary consumers of analytics outputs (executives, analysts, data scientists)?
What data governance framework exists or needs to be established?
Are there data residency requirements constraining where data can be stored?
What is the required data freshness — real-time, hourly, daily, or weekly?
Are there existing BI tools or reporting platforms that must be supported?
commonMistakes: Building a data lake without establishing data governance first, creating a data swamp
Ingesting all available data without clear use cases, wasting storage and processing costs
Not implementing data quality checks, propagating errors into downstream reports
Granting overly broad access to the lake without column-level security for sensitive data
Underestimating the ongoing operational cost of maintaining ETL pipelines and data quality
